name: PayPal
summary: PayPal is a widely recognized payment processor that lets your app accept PayPal balance, debit and credit card payments.

free_plan_covers.note: No monthly fee or user cap; you pay per transaction instead, about 3.49% plus 49 cents per US charge.

first_paid_usd_month.note: There is no monthly plan for standard PayPal Checkout; it is pay-per-transaction with no setup or monthly fees.

portability.note: PayPal's checkout and Orders API are proprietary like other processors, but its transaction history exports and huge adoption make it easier to migrate away from than a full merchant-of-record platform.

merchant_of_record.note: PayPal is a payment processor, not a merchant of record; its own Payment Services Agreement says you are responsible for determining, collecting and remitting any sales tax yourself.

subscriptions.note: PayPal supports recurring billing through its Subscriptions API, including fixed plans or amounts that scale with the number of users.

fee_summary.value: 3.49% + $0.49 per successful US card or PayPal checkout charge
fee_summary.note: That is the standard US domestic rate; PayPal adds 1.50% for international transactions and up to 4.00% when it has to convert currency.

card_fee_percent.note: PayPal keeps 3.49% of each US card payment, as listed on its pricing page.

card_fee_fixed_usd.note: On top of the percent, PayPal keeps $0.49 from each US card payment.

setup.step: Create a PayPal business account, then open the PayPal Developer Dashboard and create an app under Apps & Credentials to get a sandbox Client ID and Secret.
Set the sandbox Client ID and Secret as environment variables.
Install the PayPal JS SDK, then create an order from a server route by calling the Orders API (POST /v2/checkout/orders) with an access token generated from your Client ID and Secret.
Render the PayPal buttons on the client and capture the payment (POST /v2/checkout/orders/{orderID}/capture) once the buyer approves it.
Log in with a PayPal sandbox test buyer account to approve and complete a test payment, then swap in your live credentials when you are ready to launch.

builder_notes: Keep PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET on the server only; the client ID is meant to be public and safe to expose in the browser SDK script.
Use sandbox credentials and a sandbox buyer account while testing, and only switch to live credentials when you are ready to accept real payments.
Confirm payment by checking the order's capture status from the server, rather than trusting the client redirect alone, before marking anything as paid.
